class.name: NNDebugger
class.brief_description: Runtime side of the Noodle Nodes debugger: the root registry, snapshot and event access, and the pause/step gate.
class.description: The [b]NNDebugger[/b] engine singleton. It lists every Noodle Nodes root that is currently in the scene tree, exposes each root's snapshot, events and node properties, and forwards them to the editor over [EngineDebugger]. It also owns the process-wide pause scope and step state. The singleton only exists in a debug build of a running game. It is not registered while editing, and not registered at all in a release build, where the [NNDebugger] class and its methods are compiled out too. GDScript callers must guard every use with [code]Engine.has_singleton("NNDebugger")[/code], fetch it with [code]Engine.get_singleton("NNDebugger")[/code] and keep the result untyped: it cannot be instantiated, and variables should not be typed as it. Roots register themselves while they are in the tree. Watching a root is reference counted and starts its event recording. The editor debugger plugin subscribes to roots for you; custom tools can call [method watch], [method get_snapshot] and [method get_events] directly. Root information, snapshot and event schemas and the EngineDebugger messages are documented in [code]tutorial/Debugger_reference.md[/code]. Pausing only affects roots that step from the SceneTree's frame signals. Roots with [code]process_thread[/code] set to [code]MANUAL[/code] and direct [code]tick()[/code] calls keep running, and hosted roots follow their host. By default pausing stops only those AI ticks; see [method set_pause_scope] to pause the whole game as well.

constants.constant: Pausing stops only the scheduled Noodle Nodes ticks. The rest of the game keeps running.
Pausing stops the scheduled Noodle Nodes ticks and pauses the [SceneTree]. The tree's own pause state is restored when the debugger resumes.

method.name: diff_snapshots
method.description: Returns a delta that turns [param previous] into [param current]; [code]Protocol.apply_snapshot_delta(previous, diff)[/code] rebuilds [param current] from it. Top-level keys that differ go into [code]"set"[/code], the node array excepted. When the sequence of node [code]id[/code] and [code]parent[/code] pairs is unchanged, only the changed node entries go into [code]"nodes_changed"[/code]; otherwise the whole node array goes into [code]"nodes"[/code]. Neither argument is modified.

method.name: get_event_capacity
method.description: Returns the event ring-buffer capacity applied to every root, current and future. See [method set_event_capacity].

method.name: get_events
method.description: Returns the events recorded by the root with [param root_id] whose [code]seq[/code] is greater than [param after_seq], oldest first. Returns an empty array when the root is gone. Events are only recorded while the root is watched, and the ring buffer drops the oldest events first.

method.name: get_node_properties
method.description: Returns the current values of the properties of any live [Object] that have storage, editor or script-variable usage, keyed by property name. That includes exported and plain script variables, but not groups, categories or internal engine properties. Integer properties with an enum hint report the matching enum name (for example [code]"Multiply"[/code]) instead of the raw number, falling back to the number when no name matches; flags and other hints keep their values. Values are sanitised like [method NNBlackboard.get_debug_data], so they hold no [Object]. Returns an empty dictionary when the object is gone.

method.name: get_pause_scope
method.description: Returns the [enum PauseScope] applied by [method set_paused]. Defaults to [constant PAUSE_SCOPE_AI].

method.name: get_root_info
method.description: Returns the information dictionary of one registered root, or an empty dictionary when the root is gone. See [method get_roots] for the keys.

method.name: get_roots
method.description: Returns one information dictionary for every live registered root, in registration order. Each dictionary holds [code]id[/code], [code]type[/code] ([code]"agent"[/code], [code]"bt"[/code], [code]"st"[/code] or [code]"htn"[/code]), [code]class[/code], [code]name[/code], [code]path[/code], [code]owner_id[/code], [code]owner_name[/code], [code]owner_path[/code], [code]actor_id[/code], [code]actor_name[/code], [code]actor_path[/code], [code]host_root_id[/code], [code]host_node_id[/code], [code]host_node_name[/code] and [code]host_node_class[/code]. The owner is the scene owner; the actor is the node the root acts for, which is the one worth drawing the root against. Both come back as [code]0[/code] and empty strings when there is none, and the host fields are [code]0[/code] and empty strings for a top-level root.

method.name: get_snapshot
method.description: Returns the latest snapshot of the root with [param root_id], or an empty dictionary when the root is gone. The snapshot is built on demand and does not require watching.

method.name: is_paused
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the debugger is paused. This is the debugger's own flag; [method set_pause_scope] decides whether the [SceneTree] is paused as well. See [method set_paused].

method.name: is_watched
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the root has at least one watcher. Returns [code]false[/code] when the root is gone.

method.name: set_event_capacity
method.description: Sets the number of events each root keeps. It applies to every current root and to roots that register later. Values below [code]1[/code] clamp to [code]1[/code]. Dropping events makes gaps in the [code]seq[/code] numbers reported by [method get_events].

method.name: set_pause_scope
method.description: Sets what pausing stops. [constant PAUSE_SCOPE_AI] only pauses the scheduled AI ticks. [constant PAUSE_SCOPE_GAME] also pauses the [SceneTree]; resuming restores the pause state the tree had before the debugger paused it, so a tree the game paused itself stays paused. Changing the scope while paused applies or releases the tree pause immediately. Emits [signal pause_scope_changed]. Values other than [constant PAUSE_SCOPE_GAME] fall back to [constant PAUSE_SCOPE_AI].

method.name: set_paused
method.description: Pauses or resumes the scheduled steps of every root that steps from the SceneTree's [code]process_frame[/code] or [code]physics_frame[/code] signal. With [constant PAUSE_SCOPE_GAME] it also pauses the [SceneTree], and resuming restores the tree's previous pause state. Frames that pass while paused are dropped, so resuming does not produce a catch-up tick. Roots with [code]process_thread[/code] set to [code]MANUAL[/code] and direct [code]tick()[/code] calls are never blocked. Emits [signal paused_changed] when the state changes.

method.name: step
method.description: While paused, advances every scheduled root by one of its own frames on its process thread, then pauses again. Each root consumes its own step, so a [code]PHYSICS[/code] root and an [code]IDLE[/code] root each tick exactly once regardless of how many physics steps the next process frame contains. With [constant PAUSE_SCOPE_GAME] it also unpauses the [SceneTree] for exactly one complete frame, so one frame of ordinary node processing runs in addition to the AI tick, then pauses the tree again. Does nothing while not paused.

method.name: unwatch
method.description: Removes one watcher from the root. Event recording stops, and the recorded events are dropped, when the last watcher leaves. Unknown or freed root ids are ignored.

method.name: watch
method.description: Adds one watcher to the root and starts its event recording. Watching is reference counted, so every [method watch] must be matched by one [method unwatch]. Unknown or freed root ids are ignored.

signal.name: pause_scope_changed
signal.description: Emitted after [method set_pause_scope] changes the scope.

signal.name: paused_changed
signal.description: Emitted after [method set_paused] changes the pause state.

signal.name: root_added
signal.description: Emitted when a root enters the tree and becomes registered. [param info] has the keys documented in [method get_roots].

signal.name: root_removed
signal.description: Emitted when a registered root leaves the tree or is freed.
